sentences.zh: 春、梅諸州，炎癘頗甚，許土人領任。

translations.literal: Chun, Mei, and other prefectures have severe pestilential heat; natives are permitted to hold office.
translations.idiomatic: In Chun, Mei, and other prefectures the pestilential heat was especially severe, and natives were allowed to hold office.

sentences.zh: 景德中，令秋冬赴治，使職巡行，皆令避盛夏瘴霧之患。

translations.literal: Mid-Jingde, ordered autumn-winter administration; supervisory missions on tour were all ordered to avoid the affliction of midsummer miasma and fog.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era officials were ordered to administer in autumn and winter, and touring supervisory missions were likewise directed to avoid midsummer miasma.

translations.literal: When people fall ill they do not call doctors or take medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When people fell ill they did not call doctors or take medicine.

sentences.zh: 儋、崖、萬安三州，地狹戶少，常以瓊州牙校典治。

translations.literal: Dan, Ya, and Wan'an three prefectures have narrow territory and few households; Qiong Prefecture military adjutants commonly administer governance.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, Ya, and Wan'an were small prefectures with few households, and were commonly administered by military adjutants from Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安南數郡，土壤遐僻，但羈縻不絕而已。

translations.literal: Several commanderies of Annam have remote and distant territory; they were only kept in loose attachment without severance.
translations.idiomatic: Several commanderies of Annam lay in remote territory and were kept only in loose attachment without severance.

translations.literal: Yan Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture Circuit.

translations.literal: One prefecture (fu): Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: One prefecture: Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 州九、涿，檀，平，易，營，順，薊，景，經。

translations.literal: Nine prefectures (zhou): Zhuo, Tan, Ping, Yi, Ying, Shun, Ji, Jing, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Nine prefectures: Zhuo, Tan, Ping, Yi, Ying, Shun, Ji, Jing, and Jing.

translations.literal: Twenty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty counties.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，詔山前收復州縣，合置監司，以燕山府路為名，山后別名雲中府路。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, edict: recovered prefectures and counties south of the mountains were combined and supervisory commissioners established under the name Yan Prefecture Circuit; north of the mountains was separately named Yunzhong Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 an edict ordered that recovered prefectures and counties south of the mountains be combined under supervisory commissioners as Yan Prefecture Circuit, while territory north of the mountains was separately named Yunzhong Prefecture Circuit.

translations.literal: Yanshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐幽州，范陽郡，盧龍軍節度。

translations.literal: Tang You Prefecture, Fanyang Commandery, Lulong Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang it was You Prefecture in Fanyang Commandery, seat of the Lulong Army military governorship.

sentences.zh: 石晉以賂契丹，契丹建為南京，又改號燕京。

translations.literal: Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute; the Khitan established it as the Southern Capital and later renamed it Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute; the Khitan made it their Southern Capital and later renamed it Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 金人滅契丹，以燕京及涿、易、檀、順、景、薊六州二十四縣來歸。

translations.literal: The Jin destroyed the Khitan and returned Yanjing together with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji six prefectures and twenty-four counties.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin destroyed the Khitan, Yanjing and the six prefectures Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji with twenty-four counties were returned.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，改燕京為燕山府，又改郡曰廣陽，節度曰永清軍，領十二縣。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, changed Yanjing to Yanshan Prefecture; also changed the commandery name to Guangyang and the military governorship to Yongqing Army; administered twelve counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 Yanjing was renamed Yanshan Prefecture, its commandery was renamed Guangyang, its military governorship was renamed the Yongqing Army, and it administered twelve counties.

translations.literal: Year 5, Tong Guan and Cai You entered Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Tong Guan and Cai You entered Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 七年，郭藥師以燕山叛，金人復取之。

translations.literal: Year 7, Guo Yaoshi rebelled with Yanshan; the Jin again took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Guo Yaoshi rebelled with Yanshan, and the Jin recaptured it.

sentences.zh: 析津，宛平，都市，賜名廣寧。

translations.literal: Xijin, Wanping, Dushi, granted the name Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Xijin, Wanping, and Dushi; Dushi was granted the name Guangning.

sentences.zh: 昌平，良鄉，潞，武清，安次，永清，玉河，香河，賜名清化。

translations.literal: Changping, Liangxiang, Lu, Wuqing, Anci, Yongqing, Yuhe, Xianghe, granted the name Qinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Changping, Liangxiang, Lu, Wuqing, Anci, Yongqing, Yuhe, and Xianghe; Xianghe was granted the name Qinghua.

translations.literal: Huoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Huoyin.

translations.literal: Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金將郭藥師以州降，賜郡名曰涿水，升威行軍節度。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin general Guo Yaoshi surrendered the prefecture; granted commandery name Zhuoshui; promoted to Weixing Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin general Guo Yaoshi surrendered the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Zhuoshui and promoted to the Weixing Army military governorship.

sentences.zh: 縣四：范陽，歸義，固安，新城。

translations.literal: Four counties: Fanyang, Guiyi, Gu'an, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had four counties: Fanyang, Guiyi, Gu'an, and Xincheng.

translations.literal: Granted the name Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng was granted the name Weicheng.

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Sui; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Sui; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金人以州來歸，賜郡名曰橫山，升鎮遠軍節度。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin people returned the prefecture; granted commandery name Hengshan; promoted to Zhenyuan Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin returned the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Hengshan and promoted to the Zhenyuan Army military governorship.

translations.literal: Year 7, Jin people again captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Jin captured it again.

translations.literal: Two counties: Miyun and Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: It had two counties: Miyun and Xingtang.

translations.literal: Granted the name Weisai.
translations.idiomatic: Xingtang was granted the name Weisai.

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋置，後唐時為契丹所陷，改遼興府，以營、灤二州隸之。

translations.literal: Established under the Sui; in Later Tang captured by the Khitan, renamed Liaoxing Prefecture; Ying and Luan two prefectures were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Sui, it was captured by the Khitan in Later Tang and renamed Liaoxing Prefecture, with Ying and Luan prefectures placed under it.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，賜郡名漁陽，升撫寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, granted commandery name Yuyang; promoted to Funing Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 it was granted the commandery name Yuyang and promoted to the Funing Army military governorship.

sentences.zh: 五年，遼將張覺據州來降，尋為金所破。

translations.literal: Year 5, Liao general Zhang Jue held the prefecture and came to surrender; soon was defeated by the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Liao general Zhang Jue held the prefecture and surrendered, but was soon defeated by the Jin.

translations.literal: Three counties: Lulong, granted the name Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had three counties, beginning with Lulong, which was granted the name Lucheng.

translations.literal: Shicheng, granted the name Linguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng was granted the name Linguang.

translations.literal: Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Macheng.

translations.literal: Granted the name Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Macheng was granted the name Ancheng.

translations.literal: Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐置，雍熙四年，陷於契丹。

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Yongxi 4, fell to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang, it fell to the Khitan in Yongxi 4.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金人以州來歸，賜郡名曰遂武，防禦。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin people returned the prefecture; granted commandery name Suowu; defensive.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin returned the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Suowu and assigned defensive status.

translations.literal: Three counties: Yishui, Laishui, and Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had three counties: Yishui, Laishui, and Rongcheng.

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋置，後唐時為契丹所陷。

translations.literal: Established under the Sui; in Later Tang captured by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Sui, it was captured by the Khitan in Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，賜郡名曰平盧，防禦。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, granted commandery name Pinglu; defensive.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 it was granted the commandery name Pinglu and assigned defensive status.

translations.literal: One county: Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had one county: Liucheng.

translations.literal: Granted the name Zhenshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liucheng was granted the name Zhenshan.

translations.literal: Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shun Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金人以州來歸，賜郡名曰順興，團練。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin people returned the prefecture; granted commandery name Shunxing; regimentation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin returned the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Shunxing and assigned regimentation status.

translations.literal: One county: Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: It had one county: Huairou.

translations.literal: Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金人以州來歸，賜郡名曰廣川，團練。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin people returned the prefecture; granted commandery name Guangchuan; regimentation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin returned the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Guangchuan and assigned regimentation status.

translations.literal: Year 7, Jin people captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Jin captured it.

translations.literal: Three counties: Yuyang, granted the name Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: It had three counties, beginning with Yuyang, which was granted the name Pinglu.

translations.literal: Sanhe, Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe and Yutian.

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: It was established by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，金人以州來歸，賜郡名曰灤川，軍事。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 4, Jin people returned the prefecture; granted commandery name Luanchuan; military.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 the Jin returned the prefecture; it was granted the commandery name Luanchuan and assigned military status.

translations.literal: One county: Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: It had one county: Zunhua.

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Prefecture.

translations.literal: Originally Yutian County in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was originally Yutian County in Ji Prefecture.

translations.literal: Xuanhe 6, established as a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 6 (1124) it was established as a prefecture.

translations.literal: Year 7, fell to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year it fell to the Jin.

translations.literal: Yunzhong Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong Prefecture Circuit.

sentences.zh: 雲中府，唐雲州，大同軍節度。

translations.literal: Yunzhong Prefecture—Tang Yun Prefecture, Datong Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong Prefecture was Tang Yun Prefecture, seat of the Datong Army military governorship.

sentences.zh: 石晉以賂契丹，契丹號為西京。

translations.literal: Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute; the Khitan styled it the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute, and the Khitan styled it the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，始得雲中府、武、應、朔、蔚、奉、聖、歸、化、儒、媯等州，所謂山后九州也。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 3, Yunzhong Prefecture and the prefectures Wu, Ying, Shuo, Yu, Feng, Sheng, Gui, Hua, Ru, and Gui were first recovered—the so-called Nine Prefectures beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 3 (1121) the Song first recovered Yunzhong Prefecture and the prefectures Wu, Ying, Shuo, Yu, Fengsheng, Guihua, Ru, and Gui—the so-called Nine Prefectures beyond the mountains.

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，金人以州來歸。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 5, the Jin returned the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 5 (1123) the Jin returned the prefecture to the Song.

translations.literal: Year 6, Gujiang Fort was built.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Gujiang Fort was built.

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was again taken by the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin seized it again.

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 故屬大同軍節度，後唐置彰國軍，石晉以賂契丹。

translations.literal: Formerly under the Datong Army military governorship; Later Tang established the Zhangguo Army; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly been under the Datong Army military governorship; Later Tang established the Zhangguo Army there, and Later Jin later ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，契丹將蘇京以州來降。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 5, the Khitan general Su Jing surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 5 the Khitan general Su Jing surrendered the prefecture.

translations.literal: The Jin soon pursued Jing and retook it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin soon pursued Su Jing and retook the prefecture.

translations.literal: Shuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐置，後唐為振武軍，石晉以賂契丹。

translations.literal: Established in Tang; in Later Tang it became the Zhenwu Army; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in the Tang dynasty; Later Tang made it the Zhenwu Army, and Later Jin later ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，守將韓正以州來降。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 5, the defending general Han Zheng surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 5 the defending general Han Zheng surrendered the prefecture.

translations.literal: The Jin soon pursued Zheng and retook it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin soon pursued Han Zheng and retook the prefecture.

translations.literal: Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，守將陳翊以州來降。

translations.literal: Xuanhe 5, the defending general Chen Yi surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 5 the defending general Chen Yi surrendered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，翊為金人所殺，復取之。

translations.literal: Year 6, Yi was killed by the Jin and they retook it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chen Yi was killed by the Jin, who retook the prefecture.

translations.literal: Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐新州，後唐置威塞軍節度，石晉以賂契丹。

translations.literal: Tang Xin Prefecture; Later Tang established the Weisai Army military governorship; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It was Tang Xin Prefecture; Later Tang established the Weisai Army military governorship there, and Later Jin later ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

sentences.zh: 在雲中府之東，契丹改為奉聖州。

translations.literal: East of Yunzhong Prefecture; the Khitan renamed it Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lay east of Yunzhong Prefecture; the Khitan renamed it Fengsheng Prefecture.

translations.literal: Guihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guihua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊毅州，後唐改為武州，石晉以賂契丹，契丹改為歸化州。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Prefecture; Later Tang changed it to Wu Prefecture; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute; the Khitan renamed it Guihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Yi Prefecture; Later Tang changed it to Wu Prefecture; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute, and the Khitan renamed it Guihua Prefecture.

translations.literal: Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Prefecture.

translations.literal: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute.

translations.literal: Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐置，石晉以賂契丹，契丹改為可汗州。

translations.literal: Established in Tang; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute; the Khitan renamed it Kehan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in the Tang dynasty; Later Jin ceded it to the Khitan as tribute, and the Khitan renamed it Kehan Prefecture.
